Beginning of hostilities in the Franco-Spanish War (1635–59): Battle of Les Avins, Sack of Tienen, Siege of Leuven
Exiled Dutch nobleman René de Renesse, 1st Count of Warfusée, has the mayor of Liège, Sébastien de La Ruelle, murdered by Spanish soldiers.
Siege of Saint-Omer: French army fails to take the city of Saint-Omer
Relief of Thionville: imperial forces under Ottavio Piccolomini break the French siege of Thionville in the Duchy of Luxembourg
Army of Flanders victorious in the Battle of Honnecourt
Army of Flanders defeated in the Battle of Rocroi
Pieter and François Hemony cast the first tuned carillon
Peace of Münster ends the war with the Dutch Republic.
Archduke Leopold Wilhelm of Austria lays the foundation stone of the Capuchin church in Brussels, designed by Fr Charles of Brussels.
Jacobus de la Torre consecrates the new Capuchin church in Brussels, designed by Fr Charles of Brussels.
Battle of the Dunes: the Army of Flanders and British Royalist allies fail to raise the French-Cromwellian Siege of Dunkirk, leading to the loss of the city.
Charles II of Great Britain issues the city of Bruges with a Fisheries Privilege in gratitude for the hospitality shown him by the city during his exile.
Death of Fr Charles of Brussels at the Capuchin house in Brussels.
Marguerite Tiste, a native of Jemappes convicted of witchcraft, strangled and burned at the stake on the main square in Mons.
Death of Leonard Voeller, secretary of state for German affairs 1642-1675.
Siege of Namur
Edict in the name of Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor, reorganises office of notary in the Habsburg Netherlands.
Art school established in Brussels, later to become the Royal Academy of Fine Arts, Brussels.
Second Barrier Treaty confirms the closing of the Scheldt.
Treaty of Rastatt signed: hostilities between France and Austria arising from War of the Spanish Succession cease; Spanish Netherlands become Austrian Netherlands.
Start of Flemish China trade.
The Saint-Joseph sails from Ostend to Canton.
The Saint-Joseph reaches its home port of Ostend after a voyage to Canton, bringing a cargo of tea, porcelain, silk, and Chinese roots.
Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor grants a charter to the Ostend Company to trade with the Indies.
Work starts on Henri-Joseph Rega's new wing on the University Hall (Leuven).
Henri-Joseph Rega's new wing on the University Hall (Leuven), taken into use.
Ostend Company petitions for the harbour of Ostend to be deepened.
Ostend Company officially ceases trading in accordance with the Treaty of Vienna (1731).
Ostend Company officially wound up.
Henri-Joseph Rega establishes Leuven's botanical garden.
Henri-Joseph Rega establishes Leuven University's anatomical theatre.
Battle of Fontenoy
Siege of Brussels
Congress of Aix-la-Chapelle convenes in Aachen to negotiate an end to the War of the Austrian Succession
Privy Council grants necessary permits for artillery general Joseph de Ferraris to chart Mechelen and Brabant.
François-Charles de Velbrück establishes an academy of fine arts in Liège

Government edict regulating registration of baptisms, weddings and funerals: parish priests ordered to ensure that registrations of baptisms include the child's date of birth and the parents' places of birth; of weddings include the full names, status, place of birth and place of residence of the parties; of funerals include the date and time of death; and that a copy of each year's new entries in the parish register be deposited with the provincial authorities every January.
François-Charles de Velbrück founds the Société littéraire de Liège.
Death of Maria Theresa.
Council of Luxembourg becomes a "sovereign" court: its legal decisions can no longer be appealed to the Great Council of Mechelen.
Joseph II, Holy Roman Emperor, decrees the abolition of the Council of Brabant and the institution of new law courts for the Duchy of Brabant, to take effect from 1 May 1787.
Council of Brabant refuses to issue a new decree by Joseph II's minister plenipotentiary, Ferdinand von Trauttmansdorff.
Republic of Liège proclaimed.
Manifesto of the Province of Flanders: States of Flanders repudiate loyalty to the count of Flanders and the House of Austria and declare the old County of Flanders an independent sovereign state
Austrian military intervention restores César-Constantin-François de Hoensbroeck as prince-bishop of Liège
Battle of Jemappes: French gain control of Belgium and Liège.
Battle of Neerwinden: short-lived restoration of Austrian rule in the Low Countries.
Battle of Fleurus: decisive French victory in the Flanders Campaign of the French Revolutionary Wars.
Former Austrian Netherlands and Prince-Bishopric of Liège unilaterally annexed to the French First Republic.
Decree of 29 Prairial, Year IV establishes civil registration of births, marriages and deaths throughout what is now Belgium.
Suppression of religious life begins in earnest.
Peasants' War (Boerenkrijg) in Flanders and Brabant; peasant army defeated near Hasselt on 5 December.
Execution of Pieter Corbeels, one of the leaders of the Peasant Army, in Tournai.
Treaty of Lunéville reaffirms French annexation of the former Austrian Netherlands.
Minor Seminary, Roeselare, opens.
Napoleon Bonaparte attends the launching of the warship Friedland in Antwerp.
